content.comment_body: I'm not sure if this is the correct place to ask, but my issue may be related to the way Modbus works with [company_name] products. I am communicating with a [product_name] using [version_no] through a SCADA system, and then reading those values using a [product_name]. The system writes data in word format (16 bits), while the [product_name] handles data in byte format. I understand that 16 bits equals 2 bytes, and a double word is 4 bytes. However, when I write a single word, it seems to change three registers in the [product_name], and depending on the value, only one register may reflect the intended value until it increases. Is there a workaround for this? I haven’t mapped any registers as I intended to use the default ones. It might be that the [product_name] is reading from the wrong starting position.
In Modbus, a register consists of 16 bits, which equals 2 bytes or 1 word. If you write a single word, how do you expect the value to reflect changes across three registers?

analysis.insight_summary: A user highlights unpredictable register changes when writing one word of data from a SCADA system to a [product_name] ([version_no]), resulting in unexpected modifications across three registers in a [product_name]. The problem appears to stem from differences in data size handling between the SCADA (uses 16-bit words) and the [product_name] (operates on bytes), causing mismatched data mapping or offset problems. The user relies on default register mapping without customization, adding to confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that writing a single word from SCADA will reliably update only the intended register in the [product_name], while other registers remain unaffected, and that default register mapping should work as expected.
